renderings.value: Topic, identity and の
The は topic marker, the copula pattern, and の joining nouns - the frame every other sentence hangs off.
The copula: だ and です
Saying 'X is Y' and its past, negative and て-forms - the copula that both nouns and な-adjectives take.
Polite verb forms: ます
The polite non-past, past, negative and past-negative of verbs - the register everyday speech defaults to.
Existence and place
あります/います, plus the に and で particles that say where something is or happens.
Objects and going places
を marks what the verb acts on; に with 行く/来る/帰る/戻る marks where you are headed.
Asking questions
The core question words: who, what, where, when, which, how many.
Asking how and why
How you do something, why, and how something is said.
Someone, anyone, everyone
Question word + か for 'some-', + でも for 'any-'. One rule, applied across every question word you just learned.
Nobody, nothing, nowhere
Question word + も with a negative verb. The upstream data lists this pattern ten times over (polite and plain, three particles); it is one rule, not ten.
Adjectives
い- and な-adjectives: negative, adverbial, and the て/で forms that let them join.
い-Adjective tense and negatives
い-adjectives inflect themselves: the plain negative くない, the past かった, and the past-negative くなかった.
Making and becoming
する for a change you cause, なる for one that happens.
The て-form
The most load-bearing verb form in the language: joining clauses, ongoing action, requests. 74 later points presuppose it.
Plain verb forms: past and negative
The casual past た (same euphony as the て-form just learned), the plain negative ない, and the plain past-negative なかった.
Before, after, when
Ordering events in time, and the とき clause.
Times and approximations
から〜まで ranges, and ごろ/くらい/ぐらい for 'about'.
Wanting and being able
たい, ほしい, できる, and the こと/の nominalisers that let a whole verb phrase act as a noun.
Comparing
より, のほうが, いちばん, and asking which of two.
Listing and limiting
と, や〜など, か〜か, も, だけ, and たり〜たり.
Giving a reason
から and だから for cause. What separates them is register, not meaning.
But: one meaning, many registers
が, けど, けれど, でも, しかし, けれども all mean 'but'. The lesson is the register ladder, not six separate patterns - which is why the formal siblings from higher levels are taught here too.
Joining sentences
そして, それから and the 'well then' connectives.
Suggesting and inviting
ましょう, ませんか and the polite ways to offer.
Giving and receiving
あげる, もらう, くれる - who gives what to whom, and why Japanese cares.
How often, how much
Frequency and degree adverbs, including the あまり/ぜんぜん negatives.
Already, still, soon
もう, まだ, もうすぐ, すぐに, さっき.
Polite pointers
こちら/そちら and a few set expressions.
Plain form and experience
た ことがある and its siblings - what the plain past unlocks.
Potential, passive, causative
られる, させる, させられる - the three derived voices.
Volitional, imperative and prohibitive
The plain 'let's / I'll' volitional, the blunt imperative command, and the prohibitive な.
The ば conditional
The provisional 'if / whenever' conditional, for verbs and い-adjectives.
て-form auxiliaries
ている, てある, ておく, てしまう, てみる, ていく, てくる - the て-form's second life as an auxiliary slot.
Giving and receiving, revisited
The giving verbs again, now with their humble and honorific forms.
Doing things for people
てあげる, てくれる, てもらう - the benefactive の direction of an action.
Asking politely
The request ladder, from てくれませんか up to ていただけませんか. Pure register - the meaning never changes.
Must and may
Obligation five ways - and the five differ only by register. Plus permission and prohibition.
Advice
たほうがいい, ないほうがいい, たらいい, ばいい, といい, なさい.
Intention and purpose
つもり, ようと思う, ために, ように, and the ようにする/ようになる pair.
Guessing and hearsay
かもしれない, だろう, でしょう, ようだ, みたいだ, そうだ - how certain you are, and where you heard it.
Quoting and embedding
と思う, という, っていう, かどうか - putting a whole clause inside a sentence.
Explaining
のです/んです, ので, のに, and し for stacked reasons.
While, during, by then
ときに, 間に, までに, 中, ところ, ながら.
Verb compounds
出す, 終わる, 続ける, にくい, やすい, すぎる, 方.
Degrees and limits
ほど, より, しか〜ない, ばかり, まで, ずつ.
Changing and deciding
くする/なる, にする/なる, ことにする/ことになる - deliberate change against change that happens to you.
Even if, as it is
ても/でも, まま, and the remaining connectives.
Before (Prior To)

The whole before ladder in one place, easiest register first. These differ only by formality, so they are taught together rather than one level at a time: once you know the first, each of the rest is a one-line register fact.

Windows of time and the moment something happens
While a condition still holds, the instant one thing turns into another, and how to say something is partway done or freshly finished.
Trying, finishing, and leaving things as they are
Attempting something and failing, carrying an action through to the end, and the forms for an action left running or left undone.
Without doing, and degrees of denial
Doing one thing without another, and the adverbs and set phrases that scale a negative from 'rarely' to 'not at all' to 'not necessarily'.
Rules, habits and resolutions
Personal rules you set yourself, arrangements decided for you, and the ように forms for an effort made or an ability gained.
Drawing a conclusion, and restating it
The わけ family for what follows logically from what you just heard, plus the という forms for defining, restating and introducing a topic.
Emphasis and degree
Singling something out as precisely the one that matters, and the patterns that measure how far a quality or a situation goes.
Cause and result
Naming what caused an outcome and what followed from it, including せいで for a cause you are blaming.
Supposing, hoping, regretting
Setting up a hypothetical, wishing it had gone differently, and the forms for a hope expressed about someone else.
About, according to, compared with
The に-marked phrases that fix what a statement is about, whose standpoint it is from, and what it is measured against.
How things look, and how they stay
Pretending, resembling, and the られた form for a state that resulted from an action rather than the action itself.
Everyday spoken shortcuts
The contractions, softeners and set phrases that mark conversational N3: checking a half-remembered fact, relaying a request, offering a gentle try.

In other words, which means
The connectives that restate a statement more precisely, or draw out what it implies.
Based on, centred on, in line with
The を- and に-marked phrases that name what something was built from, organised around, or made to follow.
Worth the effort, or in vain
Whether the effort paid off: がい for something worth doing, かいがあって for effort rewarded, かいもなく for effort wasted.
Halfway, gradually, prone to
An action caught in progress, a change still underway, and the suffixes for what something tends towards or is covered in.
Can't, won't, and polite refusal
かねる for a refusal phrased as inability, and the patterns for what cannot be endured or cannot be afforded.
Torn between two options
Weighing one course against another, and the forms for a wish that something could be made possible.
Precisely because, and just because
からこそ for a reason you are insisting on, からといって for one you are rejecting, and the からsurrounding judgements in between.
As you would expect of it
だけあって for something living up to its reputation, にかけては for where someone excels, and the patterns for a saving grace.
Far from it, let alone that
どころか and its neighbours: correcting an assumption by overshooting it, and setting one thing aside to get to another.
Along with, in step with
Two things moving together, one following the other, and the markers for what preceded or triggered an event.
Reacting, feeling, finding it unbearable
ことに for the feeling a fact provokes, ものがある for an impression you cannot name, and the forms for excess and indifference.
Not without, not unless
The double-negative conditions: what cannot happen until something else does, and what has to be got out of the way first.

Whether one or the other
The paired literary patterns for listing alternatives, and for admitting you cannot tell which of them applies.
Two things at once, two things alike
Doing one thing alongside another, roles held together, and the matched pairs that say two facts are of a piece.
Only this, and nothing else
ならでは for what only one thing can offer, をおいて他に for the one remaining candidate, and the patterns that dismiss the alternatives.
Scale, quantity and extent
からある for a figure you are stressing as large, というところだ for one you are playing down, and the suffixes for entirety.
From whose standpoint, on what grounds
The literary からの/から言わせれば forms for whose view a statement is, and the phrases that name the basis it rests on.
Granted that, but
こそ paired with a contrast: conceding one point emphatically in order to deny another.
As if, seeming like, putting it on
The ごとく simile forms, the ぶる family for affecting a manner, and the suffixes for something that merely looks the part.
It's not as if, it won't do
あるまいし for dismissing a premise, ではすまない for what cannot be left at that, and the forms for a duty that will not go away.
Befitting the position, or not
たる for the standing something holds, ともあろう and にあるまじき for conduct that falls short of it.
Turning points and starting points
The moment a situation changed: を境に for the pivot, を皮切りに for the first of a series, を経て for the process passed through.
Forced into it, and the state it left
を余儀なくされる for a course forced on you, 始末だ for where it ended up, and the literary suffixes and exclamations for an extreme.
Unfazed by it, aside from it
をものともせずに for pressing on regardless, をよそに for ignoring it, はさておき for setting it aside.
No end to it
The きりがない patterns for something that cannot be exhausted, and ては/そばから for a cycle that keeps restarting.
Without doing, without meaning to
The literary 'without' forms, ずじまい for a chance missed, and ともなく for something done without intending it.
Not impossible, not unheard of
The hedged double negatives that concede a possibility without endorsing it, the literary potential form, and べからず for a flat prohibition.
Worth it, or unbearable
に堪える and に堪えない for what does or does not repay the attention, 足る and 足りない for what measures up.
When it comes to that
The となると/となれば family for a situation reaching a threshold, and the conditionals that follow from it.
Depending on how it turns out
The のいかん set: one noun, three grammatical slots, all saying the outcome hangs on this.
Naming a thing, and seeing it through
The という forms that name or generalise, ぬく for carrying something through to the end, and the phrases for what you did it in spite of.
